project.scope: Make the approved Riverbend Tool Library frontend work: membership, a real collection behind the catalogue's filters, reservations with conflict checking, and the two-sided message thread between members and the desk. The design is finished and must not change.

runtime.deploy: static frontend plus a local API process

evidence: reservations that survive restarting the application

dataModels.purpose: One row per membership. Email is unique. `role` is member or staff; `status` is applied, active or lapsed.
An issued session. The cookie carries this id and nothing else.
The lending collection. This is what the catalogue's filters and search operate on.
One booking of one item by one member. `status` is reserved, out, returned, overdue or cancelled. `member_id` is the owner.
A two-sided thread per member. `author` is member or staff. A member's thread is their own.

apis.purpose: Create a membership application. Refuses an email already registered.
Issue a session. The same 401 for an unknown email and a wrong password.
Who the session belongs to and the role, so the navigation can take its signed-in shape.
The whole collection with each item's current availability. This is the list the catalogue's filters, search, sort and counts already operate on.
One item, so the item page can resolve the id in its query string.
Whether an item is free between two dates. The reservation wizard's second step asks this.
Record a reservation, refusing dates that clash with an existing one.
The signed-in member's OWN reservations. Never anyone else's.
Cancel a reservation the caller owns. Another member's is refused with 403.
The signed-in member's own thread, both sides of it.
Add a member message to their own thread.
Reservations waiting to be handed out. A member session is refused with 403.
The collection with loan state, for the desk.
Hand out, return or cancel any reservation. Staff only.
Unanswered member messages across all threads. Staff only.
Reply on one member's thread. The reply must appear on that member's own thread and on no other.

securityControls.requirement: A password is never stored or logged in a readable form. Only a hash is kept.
evidence: no column holding a plaintext password

securityControls.requirement: Every read and write of a reservation is scoped to the caller's own membership, on the server.
evidence: member_id compared against the session on the server

securityControls.requirement: A member sees their own message thread and no one else's, decided on the server. A thread is two-sided, so the staff replies on it are theirs to see and other members' are not.
evidence: member_id from the session, never from the request

securityControls.requirement: Every staff endpoint refuses a member session outright. An empty list is not a refusal: it is indistinguishable from a quiet day, which is how a hole stays hidden.
evidence: a role check before any staff data is read

securityControls.requirement: The session cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite.
No credential, hash or session secret appears in anything the browser downloads.
evidence: the built assets contain no secret

operations.behaviour: Create a membership application from the form and show the approved errors when the email is taken or a field is wrong.
acceptance: a valid application creates exactly one row in members with a hashed password and status 'applied'
an email that is already a member is refused with 422 and creates no second row
a password under 12 characters is refused with 422 and nothing is stored
the stored password_hash is not the password

operations.behaviour: Sign in and issue a session cookie, with one message for any failure.
acceptance: correct credentials are accepted and a session cookie is set HttpOnly
a wrong password is refused with 401 and no session is issued
an unknown email is refused with the same 401 and the same message
GET /api/me returns the member and their role

operations.behaviour: Serve the collection with each item's availability, so the approved filters, search, sort and per-category counts have something to work on. The filtering itself already works in the browser and must not be moved to the server.
acceptance: the catalogue lists every item that is not retired
each item reports an availability of in, out or soon derived from its reservations
a retired item never appears
the per-category counts in the approved sidebar match the items returned

operations.behaviour: Resolve the id in the page's query string to one item, and show the approved not-found state when it does not exist.
acceptance: a known id returns that item's name, category, condition and deposit
an unknown id is answered 404 and the page shows its not-found state rather than an error
a retired item is answered 404

operations.behaviour: Answer whether an item is free between two dates, which the wizard's second step asks before it offers to confirm.
acceptance: dates that clash with an existing reservation are reported as unavailable
dates that do not clash are reported as available
a return date before the collection date is refused with 422
a loan longer than seven days is refused with 422

operations.behaviour: Record the reservation and confirm it in the approved style. Refuse a clash rather than double-booking.
acceptance: a reservation on free dates is stored with status 'reserved' and the signed-in member as owner
a reservation clashing with an existing one is refused with 422 and nothing is stored
two identical requests sent together result in exactly one reservation
reserving while unauthenticated is refused with 401

operations.behaviour: List the signed-in member's own reservations in the approved table, with the approved empty state when there are none.
acceptance: the list contains only reservations whose member_id is the signed-in member
an unauthenticated request is refused with 401
a member with none sees the empty state, not an error
requesting the list as one member never returns another member's row

operations.element: the Cancel button in a reservations row
operations.behaviour: Cancel a reservation the signed-in member owns and reflect it in the table.
acceptance: cancelling an own reservation sets its status to 'cancelled' and persists
cancelling another member's reservation is refused with 403 and leaves it unchanged
cancelling an item already handed out is refused with 422
the cancelled dates become available again

operations.behaviour: Show the signed-in member's own thread, both their messages and the desk's replies.
acceptance: the thread contains only messages whose member_id is the signed-in member
staff replies on that member's thread are visible to them
another member's thread is never returned
an unauthenticated request is refused with 401

operations.behaviour: Add the member's message to their own thread and show it in the approved style.
acceptance: a submitted message is stored against the signed-in member with author 'member'
an empty message is refused with 422 and nothing is stored
a member cannot write a message onto another member's thread
the member_id is taken from the session and never from the request body

operations.element: the queue, collection and enquiries panels
operations.behaviour: Serve the three staff views: reservations waiting to be handed out, the collection with loan state, and unanswered enquiries, with the approved counts above them.
acceptance: a staff session receives the queue, the collection and the enquiries
a member session is refused with 403 for each of them, not handed an empty list
an unauthenticated request is refused with 401
the three counts shown match the rows actually stored

operations.element: the Hand out button and the reply forms
operations.behaviour: Hand out, return or cancel any reservation, and reply on a member's thread. Both are staff-only and both must be visible to the member they concern.
acceptance: a staff session can hand out a reservation and the change persists
a staff reply appears on that member's own thread and on no other member's
a member session attempting either is refused with 403 and nothing changes
an unknown status value is refused with 422

outOfScope: No payment is taken: the £35 membership fee is settled at the desk and nothing here handles money.
No email or SMS is sent. Confirmations and replies appear in the interface only.
No real member data. Everything is fictional.
Nothing is deployed. The finished application runs locally for verification.

missing.what: How a staff membership comes to exist
missing.why: Joining creates a member. Promoting one to staff is an administrative act and the approved design has no screen for it.
The approved design has no screen for adding an item, only for editing one. Where the four hundred tools come from is not something the frontend says.
